content.intro: This lesson focuses on asynchronous processing for performance in caching, conditional requests, and performance. You will connect background job queues to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous Processing for Performance matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying background job queues deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Caching and validators can reduce work and prevent stale reads or lost updates, but cache policy must protect sensitive representations. In this lesson, treat “Asynchronous Processing for Performance” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.

common_mistakes: Treating asynchronous processing for performance as an implementation detail rather than a documented behavior.
Testing only the happy path and ignoring malformed, unauthorized, conflicting, duplicate, or dependency-failure cases.
Publishing an example without checking version assumptions, sensitive-data exposure, and the expected output.
